title: In the Bleak Midwinter
description: Christina Rossetti's Christmas poem to Gustav Holst's tune Cranham, in Holst's own four parts from The English Hymnal (1906), for 2 to 4 singers: the first, second and last of her five verses, at Holst's moderate pace. Every line ends on a rest for a breath, and the last verse asks "What can I give him" and answers "Give my heart."

credits.arrangement: Gustav Holst's four parts (The English Hymnal, 1906), adapted by Stackapella

licence.words: public domain: Christina Georgina Rossetti died 1894; her poem's earliest known printing is "A Christmas Carol", Scribner's Monthly, vol. 3 (New York, November 1871 to April 1872), p. 278, illustrated, all five verses; sung as The English Hymnal prints it (No. 25, all five verses), verses 1, 2 and 5, the dash after the last "give him" written as a comma
licence.tune: public domain: first printed in The English Hymnal (1906), whose preface names "Mr. G. von Holst (25, 310, 571)" among "those who have composed tunes especially for this collection"; Gustav Holst died 1934
licence.arrangement: Holst's own four parts as printed with the tune (Holst died 1934; the book's musical editor, Ralph Vaughan Williams, died 1958, is named for the edition only), his tune, chords and key, with these changes for 2 to 4 beginners: on "bleak mid-" (bars 1, 5 and 13) the alto sings E4 then D4 and the tenor A3, A3 (Holst F4, C4 in the alto and C4, F3 in the tenor) so the duet has a sixth under the tune's C and the chords are A minor, then D minor on F, where Holst has F on A, then F; in bars 5 and 13 the tenor starts on C4 (Holst F3); on "Fros-ty wind made" (bar 3) the alto sings B-flat3, D4, B-flat3, C4 (Holst D4, D4, D4, C4) so the duet has G minor's third, and the tenor holds G3 (Holst G3, D3, D3); "moan" (bar 4) is one note a syllable: alto E4 (Holst C4), tenor G3 (Holst F3 to E3), bass C3 (Holst G2 to C3); on "Wa-ter like a" (bar 7) the alto sings B-flat3, D4, E4, C4 and the tenor F3, F3 (Holst F4, F4, E4, F4 and D4, D4), so the duet has no second under the tune's G, and on "stone" (bar 8) the alto takes A3 for Holst's unison F4; in bar 9 the alto sings D4, C4, D4, F4 (Holst F4, F4, F4, E-flat4), the last beat an F chord on C passing down the bass where Holst has F7 on C (its E-flat would have risen); in bar 10 the alto holds F4 (Holst D4) so the duet has no octave under the D5s; where the tune sings two notes to a syllable (bars 11 and 15) the lower parts hold one note: alto E4, D4, tenor C4, B-flat3, bass A2, B-flat2 in bar 11 (Holst F4-E4, D4; F3-C4, B-flat3-A3); alto D4, E4, tenor B-flat3, B-flat3, bass B-flat2, C3 in bar 15 (Holst F4, E4-F4; D4, B-flat3-A3; B-flat2, C3-F3), the last verse's tenor F3, C3 there; the last bar of each verse has the alto on A3 where Holst's alto and tune meet on F4, and the song's last chord is F4, A3, C3, F2 (Holst F4, F4, A3, F3) so it has its root, third and fifth; breaths: Holst's own crotchet rests; verse 1's last "go." is cut to two beats and verse 2's "Christ." to three, for the breath before the next verse; the other verses fitted to the notes: verse 2's first half as the book's own "Verses 2 and 3 run" ("Our" a crotchet pickup on A4; "heaven" one syllable; "Nor" over G and A; "flee a-way" G dotted crotchet, G quaver, F, with "way" a crotchet before the breath where the book has a minim); "win-ter A" as the two D5s tied, "ter" a quaver, a breath, and "A" a quaver pickup on A4, as the book's run makes its pickups from the note before; "Je-sus" and "Give my" as "Long a-"; in the last verse "What" on the dotted A, "him" over G and F, "wise" on the two D5s tied, and "I give him" splitting the G minim, as the book's run does for "Che-ru-bim"; accepted: the duet sings the tune's G over the alto's D for a beat or two before the tune falls to F over D (Holst's suspension on "win-ter", "i-ron", "shep-herd" and the like, and the G on "on", "place", "do" and on "Long", "Je-", "Give"), as every B-flat3 there would make a tritone or a parallel; and the alto's last move, E4 down to A3, gives the duet's last chord its third without crossing the tune; the tenor sings Holst's own line in the last two bars of verse 5, as in verses 1 and 2, and the bass takes D3 under "moan", "tain" and "am?" (bar 4 of each verse), so the outer parts move in contrary motion there. Accepted: the duet's D4 under the tune's C4 on "made" (bar 3), Holst's alto, the seventh of D minor; and the alto holding E4 under the tune's passing F4 for half a beat before each verse's last note; the octaves and fifths the app notes at the start of each line (beats 8, 16, 24, 40, 48 and their repeats, and each verse's opening) come across the breath that ends the line before, where Holst's parts start their next line, and are not heard as consecutive.
licence.source: The English Hymnal with Tunes (London: Henry Frowde, Oxford University Press, and A. R. Mowbray; undated, the Frowde imprint of 1906 to 1913, the preface dated Ascension Day 1906 and its music preface signed "R. Vaughan Williams, Musical Editor"), No. 25, "Cranham. (Irreg.)", "In moderate time, crotchet = 100", "G. von Holst", p. 44 (the music, with "Verses 2 and 3 run" beneath it) and p. 45 (the five verses, headed "Christina G. Rossetti, 1830-94"), in four parts in F, 4/4, written here in F in 4/4 as printed; read from the scan at archive.org/details/englishhymnalwit0000unse_b6d2 (page/n75 and n76); the same music compared with a later printing (London: Humphrey Milford, Oxford University Press, undated, the composer "G. Holst"), p. 44, archive.org/details/englishhymnalwit00unse/page/n77; both printings misprint verse 5's "Poor as I am?" as "Pcor", sung here as "Poor"; "sufficed" without a stop, as printed.
